answer_html: Zola puts the average 2026 wedding at $36,000, with 145 guests on average. Scaled from its national averages, the venue takes 18% ($6,582), catering 15%, flowers and décor 14%, the bar 12%, photography 9% and the dress 4% ($1,535). Type your own budget below.

faq.q: Is $10,000 a good budget for a wedding?
faq.a: It is 28% of Zola's $36,000 average for 2026, so every line is smaller: scaled from Zola's national averages, $10,000 gives the venue $1,828, catering $1,477 and the dress $427. Real prices fit it: courthouse fees from $60 (New York), a chapel for the couple from $197 and secondhand designer gowns from $65 (each checked Oct 28, 2026). Type $10,000 above to see all 15 lines.

faq.q: What is a realistic budget for a small wedding?
faq.a: Zola's 2026 couples spend $36,000 on average for 145 guests: about $248 a guest. A small wedding can cost far less. Elopement and micro wedding packages in our five cities start at $350 ($159 in Las Vegas), and the cheapest room with a printed price for up to 80 guests in New York is $595 (checked Oct 28, 2026). Type your budget and guest count above.

faq.q: What is a reasonable budget for a wedding dress?
faq.a: Zola's 2026 national average is $2,000 for the dress plus $550 for alterations: together 5.4% of the 15 items it lists, or $1,957 on a $36,000 budget. Secondhand designer gowns cost less: the 30 we re-opened on Oct 28, 2026 run from $65 to $1,000 on Poshmark.

faq.q: What is a normal cost for a wedding venue?
faq.a: Zola's 2026 national average for the venue and site fees is $8,573, with a typical range of $6,900 to $10,300; it is the biggest line, 18% of the split. Small rooms that print their price start much lower: $197 in Houston and $250 in Dallas (chapels for the couple), $320 in Los Angeles (up to 5 guests), $400 in Chicago (up to 100) and $595 in New York (up to 80): the cheapest in each city, checked Oct 28, 2026.

faq.q: How is a wedding budget usually broken down?
faq.a: Scaled from Zola's 2026 national averages: venue 18%, catering 15%, flowers and décor 14%, bar 12%, photography 9%, wedding planning 9%, videography 9% and the dress 4%. Music, hair and makeup, cake, alterations, invitations, the officiant and the tux take the last 11%. The honeymoon and the rings are paid outside the day and are not in the split.
